checks.lead: Arius (; Koine Greek: Ἄρειος, romanized: Áreios; 250 or 256 – 336) was a Cyrenaic presbyter and ascetic who became the central catalyst for the Arian controversy. Long regarded within mainstream Christian tradition as the archetypal heretic—demonized in early medieval art and polemic alongside figures like Judas—he was historically cast as the singular architect of a radical departure from orthodoxy.
